To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
distributed transmit mode selection with limited feedback is an efficient and robust technique for multi-user MISO broadcast channels.

a distributed adaptive transmit mode switching strategy, in which the transmitter selects between single-user and multiuser transmission based on limited feedback from the users, is shown to achieve significant sum-rate gains over single-mode transmission for low to moderate numbers of users.

a distributed transmit mode switching algorithm, based on local CSIT, statistical knowledge, and limited feedback, achieves significant throughput gains over TDMA for a low to moderate number (up to 10) of users and linear rate growth in the interference limited region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the design and optimization of adaptive transmission schemes in wireless networks with limited feedback.
a fundamental question in multi-user information theory: How can we design distributed algorithms to optimally allocate resources among users in multi-user networks with limited CSIT and feedback?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed scheme provides a simple and effective way to improve the performance of multiuser MISO broadcast channels.
our proposed scheme achieves near optimal sum rate with low complexity and limited feedback.
our proposed scheme is a promising approach for the design of future wireless systems, which is capable of exploiting the benefits of SDMA and TDMA, while maintaining low feedback overhead.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed scheme is able to achieve the same performance as the optimal mode selection scheme with full CSI at the base station, but without any CSI feedback.
we propose a novel distributed transmit mode selection scheme, where each user feeds back its CQI and mode decision.

the distributed mode selection scheme with limited feedback provides a practical solution to the problem of multiuser scheduling in the presence of limited CSIT, which is of great importance for future wireless networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
distributed mode selection with limited feedback can provide substantial performance gains for the MISO BC with more users than antennas.
, in a broadcast network with more users than antennas, it is beneficial for the base station to dynamically select between TDMA and SDMA.
, in the presence of limited feedback, the base station can exploit the statistical knowledge of the non-local information to improve the sum-rate performance of the system.
